title: Pre-hospital tranexamic acid pathway in a rural emergency network: compliance, timing and the limits of unlinked data
subtitle: Design undecided: pathway compliance audit, linked outcome analysis, or both
statement: Paramedics in a rural network have carried tranexamic acid for adults with suspected major bleeding after injury since 2023, to be given within three hours of injury, but nobody knows how many eligible patients receive it, how quickly, or whether treated patients do better. Ambulance records can be reviewed now; hospital outcomes cannot be linked while the data-sharing agreement is lapsed.
whoAffected: Injured adults with suspected major bleeding in a large rural area, especially patients attended by single paramedics or facing long transport times; paramedics; the three hospitals' emergency and trauma teams.
whatHurts: A patient who bleeds without timely tranexamic acid loses a treatment that works best early; a patient given it after three hours may gain nothing and risk harm. Without data the network cannot tell where the pathway fails.
currentPractice: Paramedics decide on tranexamic acid from protocol criteria; no audit of eligibility, timing or outcomes has been done since the drug was introduced.
whyNow: The pathway has run for three years, crews report missed and late doses, and the audit committee has approved a review of ambulance records.
constraints: No funding; the work fits existing clinical governance time. Ambulance records can be reviewed only by the ambulance service's audit team. Hospital outcome data cannot be linked until a data-sharing agreement is in place.
patientCenteredGoal: Every injured patient who is bleeding receives tranexamic acid early when it can help, and nobody receives it late when it cannot.
summary: Problem framed around compliance and timing, with outcome questions dependent on data linkage that is not currently allowed.
